classification: New measurement and workload-definition extension; existing benchmark and results remain frozen
decision_order: Protocol written before selecting candidate anchors or obtaining writer outputs
motivation: Characterize operations beyond direct identifier-chain traversal and separate operator coverage from linguistic variants and real engineer-question demand

prior_work.comparison: SemBench explicitly varies operators and scenarios. The existing primary PDF was directly read by reviewers; this pilot adds operator coverage within the present source-bound process resource, rather than claiming a novel general robustness technique.
Dr.Spider already studies natural-question, database and SQL perturbations. Paraphrase robustness is established prior work; merely renaming or multiplying templates is not a new contribution.

operators.semantics: For one CR pack, count distinct member documents per source-verified whole-document disposition code; document may contribute to multiple code groups if records contain several codes.
operators.eligibility: At least two distinct members with a verified whole-document disposition

operators.semantics: Intersection of typed section identities modified by two documents within one pack; output specification, release and clause.
operators.eligibility: Two members with at least one common section identity and at least one section outside their intersection

operators.semantics: Typed sections modified by the first document and absent from the second document's typed modifications; output specification, release and clause.
operators.eligibility: Same pair rule as shared_clauses, oriented lexically, with nonempty first-minus-second

operators.semantics: Among members of one pack, return documents whose typed modifications include both of two specified section identities.
operators.eligibility: Distinct sections that co-occur for at least one member, and at least one other member has only one of them

operators.semantics: Among all member documents in a pack, return every document tied for the maximum count of distinct modified typed section identities, together with that count.
operators.eligibility: At least two pack members and at least two different positive clause-footprint counts

operators.semantics: Return member documents for which the released records contain zero typed modified-section links. This is recorded-link absence in this snapshot.
operators.eligibility: Pack contains at least one member with links and one member without links

selection: One eligible anchor per operator and partition, smallest SHA256 of study label, WG, family and complete candidate identity. Freeze all candidates and chosen identities before writer execution. Record unavailable cells, without substituting a different operator.
gold: Derive with independent Python sets/dictionaries from raw relation rows, then check a separately written SQL reference. Equal row-set results are required for admission. Original source-audit scopes remain unchanged.
questions: Author-written questions with distinct surface forms and explicit requested fields; label authored, not collected user questions. Independently check question/SQL/gold semantic agreement before writer execution.
writer_condition: Fresh Codex session receives schema, complete relevant value domains and questions only; no gold, reference SQL, prior model outputs or execution feedback. One first response per question. No paid API. Run generated SELECT queries read-only with the same fixed runtime and 60-second cap. Preserve all outcomes; no retry for higher accuracy.
analysis: Per-operator and per-WG exact row sets, errors and timeouts; pairwise gold/ref equality, input/output hashes and all selection exclusions. Interpret as a balanced small authored operator pilot, with its session count; no claim of human question distribution or causal operator effect.
publication_gate: Include new study in public prose only after independent semantic validation, actual execution, original-input hash checks and an immutable replay bundle. Preserve unhelpful results internally and decide inclusion by whether the study addresses the stated question, not whether accuracy improves.
